title: Fynaptix · Quantum Computing Research
heading: Quantum Computing Intelligence
subheading: Pure-plays, hedged giants & the road to commercial advantage
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Quantum pure-plays trade at extreme valuations (P/S ~73–568×) and are highly speculative — position sizing matters more here than anywhere else on this hub. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: A reversal from last week's broad rally: IonQ jumped 16.2% to $45.48 (Sep 25) on its FY26 guidance raise, and the Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM) rebounded 7.7% to $153.72. But Quantinuum gave back 9.1% to $49.53 and Pasqal fell another 12.0% to $6.99, while Rigetti (+3.5% to $16.66) and D-Wave (+1.8% to $17.41) were roughly flat. The sector split this week rather than moving as a block.

IonQ raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $450–460 million (from $280–290 million, +60% at the midpoint, reported Sep 17) on its SkyWater Technology foundry acquisition, which closed July 31 and is expected to contribute roughly $240M of revenue over the final five months of 2026. The raise cuts IonQ's forward price-to-sales to roughly 40× from its ~73× trailing multiple.

IonQ $45.48 (~$18.07B mkt cap / $246.5M TTM revenue, P/S ~73× trailing — set to compress toward ~40× on its new FY26 guidance) / Rigetti $16.66 (~$5.56B / $13.4M TTM, P/S ~417×) / D-Wave $17.41 (~$6.48B / ~$12–13M TTM, P/S ~514×) / Quantinuum $49.53 (~$13.0B mkt cap / $22.97M TTM revenue, P/S ~568×, still against just $28–32M FY26 guidance); Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM) $153.72 (Sep 25, +7.7% on the week), still below its 52-week high of $170

tiers.label: Hedged Giants — Quantum as an Option
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: A quieter week after last week's $1B Anderon CHIPS finalization: IBM partnered with Q-CTRL on its Quantum Nighthawk r2 platform to push execution speed, and its Q4Bio challenge awarded $2M to Algorithmiq, Cleveland Clinic and IBM itself for 100-qubit photodynamic-therapy simulations
rows.watch for: Yield and qualification ramp at the Albany 300mm foundry line; further Nighthawk r2 adoption; progress toward IBM's broader $10B quantum commercialization pledge

rows.angle: Google Quantum AI announced a genuine logical-qubit stability milestone (Sep 22) — refined parity-check cycles let a logical qubit outlast the physical qubits that compose it, a real step beyond NISQ-era hardware — ending a run of quiet weeks on Willow-specific progress
rows.watch for: Integration of stable logical qubits into larger interconnected arrays; UK NQCC access-program results; any competitive response to IBM's foundry buildout or NVIDIA's platform push

rows.angle: Microsoft opened a new quantum research center in Maryland (Sep 22) with the University of Maryland and handed its Majorana 2 topological-qubit system to DARPA for independent, on-site testing — a step toward third-party validation of claims outside physicists still debate
rows.watch for: DARPA's independent test results; Quantinuum partnership developments ahead of Quantum World Congress; any reproducibility findings on the Majorana approach

rows.angle: A comparatively quiet week directly from NVIDIA, but its CUDA-Q ecosystem kept widening: Infleqtion advanced fault-tolerant tooling on CUDA-Q Logical, and Quantum Machines paired NVQLink with new AMD-based control hardware
rows.watch for: Further CUDA-Q Logical adoption across labs and hardware partners; confirmation of NVentures' reported QuEra investment; additional NVQLink integrations beyond Quantum Machines

tiers.label: Pure-Plays — Highly Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list. Most quantum systems remain in R&D; true commercial systems are likely years away.

rows.angle: The week's standout mover: IonQ raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $450–460M (from $280–290M, +60% at the midpoint, reported Sep 17) on its SkyWater Technology foundry acquisition (closed Jul 31), while also demonstrating a CPU-only real-time quantum error decoder and a quantum-generative-modeling radar application
rows.watch for: Shares rose ~16% to $45.48 (Sep 25); the guidance raise cuts forward P/S to ~40× from ~73× trailing; SkyWater integration progress and delivery on Superion 256 orders

rows.angle: A quiet week: shares added ~3.5% to $16.66, tracking broad sector sentiment rather than new company-specific news. The DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage B exclusion confirmed last week still stands
rows.watch for: Any renewed path into QBI Stage B via separate negotiation; consensus target ~$28.53 (Buy); P/S ~417×, still among the richest in the sector

rows.angle: New independent analysis (Trefis, Sep 23) sharpens the risk picture: shares are down ~61% from their 52-week high without any market-wide shock, the $6.48B market cap rests almost entirely on future potential against $3.1M of quarterly revenue, and adjusted EBITDA losses widened 85% YoY to $37.1M
rows.watch for: D-Wave's dual-platform (annealing + gate-model) showcase at Quantum World Congress (Sep 23–25); consensus target ~$34.65 (Strong Buy) despite the overhangs; cash runway of $546.2M as of June 2026

rows.angle: Shares fell another ~12% to $6.99 (Sep 25) — a new post-IPO low, roughly 63% below the Aug 28 debut-day close — despite H1 2026 revenue growth of 14% YoY and a ~$355.8M cash raise from the listing
rows.watch for: First full reporting quarter as a listed company; any stabilization after three-plus weeks of steady declines; deployment of IPO proceeds into sales and R&D expansion

private_watchlist.name: PsiQuantum
private_watchlist.note: Finalized its own $100M CHIPS R&D award with the Commerce Department (Sep 8) targeting photonic-quantum manufacturing challenges — electro-optic materials, high-temperature single-photon detectors and ultra-low-loss photonic packaging. Continues building out its Moreton Bay Central fault-tolerant facility in Australia on top of its ~$10.5B private valuation (~$1.5B round, May 2026).

private_watchlist.name: Quantinuum
private_watchlist.note: Shares fell ~9% to $49.53 (Sep 25), giving back most of the prior week's rally, even as Quantinuum finalized its own $100M CHIPS R&D award and detailed new Oracle and Quanta Computer commercialization partnerships ahead of Quantum World Congress (Sep 23–25). FY26 revenue guidance remains just $28–32M against a market cap now closer to $13.0B.

private_watchlist.name: QuEra
private_watchlist.note: Continues building on its 96 verified logical qubits (Nature) and confirmed DARPA QBI Stage B slot. A QuEra-commissioned survey released this week found 45% of enterprise quantum buyers now prioritize fault-tolerance roadmaps (second only to cost), with neutral atoms the preferred architecture (23%) ahead of superconducting qubits (15%) — a data point in QuEra's favor, coming from QuEra itself.

bear_case.title: Years from commercial advantage
bear_case.description: Roughly half of IonQ's dramatic new FY26 guidance ($450–460M) is inorganic — it comes from the SkyWater Technology semiconductor foundry it acquired, not organic quantum-computing revenue. D-Wave's own Q2 revenue was just $3.08M, a reminder of how small the underlying pure-play businesses still are.

bear_case.title: A rally doesn't erase execution risk
bear_case.description: Quantinuum fell ~9% and Pasqal fell ~12% this week despite real, positive company news for both (new Oracle/Quanta partnerships for Quantinuum; continued revenue growth for Pasqal) — a sign that September's speculative repricing can reverse just as fast for names without a hard catalyst behind the move.

bear_case.title: Insiders aren't buying — and the number keeps growing
bear_case.description: Insiders at IonQ, Rigetti and D-Wave have sold a net of roughly $988M in stock over the trailing five years, with no offsetting insider buying reported this week — and IonQ's own CEO sold another ~$598,000 of shares (Sep 11), even if framed as routine tax-withholding on vesting stock.

bear_case.title: Cash burn, not just multiples, is the real risk
bear_case.description: Trefis's Sep 23 analysis of D-Wave puts a number on it: a $6.48B market cap resting almost entirely on future potential, adjusted EBITDA losses that widened 85% year-over-year to $37.1M, and a historical worst-case drawdown of roughly 97% across the sector's five market shocks since 2022 — before the next dilutive raise.

bear_case.title: The winner may not be listed — or may be a giant's subsidiary
bear_case.description: PsiQuantum's own $100M CHIPS R&D award (finalized Sep 8) and QuEra's continued private-market progress reinforce that a meaningful share of the technology roadmap sits outside anything an investor can buy directly as a pure-play — alongside IBM's Anderon, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary, not a separate stock.

catalysts.title: Quantum World Congress
catalysts.description: D-Wave showcased its dual-platform (annealing plus gate-model) strategy alongside Quantinuum and IonQ presentations — the sector's highest-profile event of the month.

catalysts.title: Microsoft hands Majorana 2 to DARPA for independent testing
catalysts.description: A new Maryland quantum research center, built with the University of Maryland, gives DARPA hands-on, on-site access to Microsoft's topological-qubit system for outside verification.

catalysts.title: Google Quantum AI's logical-qubit stability milestone
catalysts.description: Refined parity-check cycles let a logical qubit maintain its state longer than the physical qubits composing it — a concrete step toward fault tolerance, though still confined to the lab.

catalysts.title: IonQ raises FY26 revenue guidance to $450–460M
catalysts.description: Up from $280–290M (+60% at the midpoint), driven by the SkyWater Technology foundry acquisition that closed July 31; shares extended their rebound to $45.48.

catalysts.title: D-Wave confirms its Quantum World Congress showcase
catalysts.description: Detailed plans to present both its annealing and gate-model architectures, underscoring its dual-technology bet ahead of the conference.

catalysts.title: PsiQuantum finalizes its $100M CHIPS R&D award
catalysts.description: Commerce Department funding targets photonic-quantum manufacturing challenges: electro-optic materials, high-temperature single-photon detectors and ultra-low-loss photonic packaging.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: IBM
positions.note: A quieter week after last week's $1B Anderon CHIPS finalization: a Q-CTRL/IBM Nighthawk r2 partnership and a $2M Q4Bio challenge award are incremental, not transformative. Trimmed a few points to fund this week's much stronger IonQ catalyst; still the largest position on the strength of its $10B+ committed roadmap.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: Google Quantum AI's Sep 22 logical-qubit stability milestone — a logical qubit now outlasting the physical qubits that compose it — is genuine technical substance that ends a run of quiet weeks on Willow-specific hardware. Nudged up on that basis; also your largest AI-sleeve holding, so size this weight with that overlap in mind.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Microsoft opened a new Maryland quantum center and handed its Majorana 2 chip to DARPA for independent on-site testing (Sep 22) — a real step toward third-party validation, though physicists quoted in this week's coverage still debate the underlying topological-qubit claims. Held steady pending that independent read; also held in the AI sleeve — avoid double-counting.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: A quieter week directly from NVIDIA, but its CUDA-Q ecosystem kept widening as Infleqtion advanced fault-tolerant tooling and Quantum Machines paired NVQLink with new AMD control hardware. Held roughly steady — ecosystem breadth keeps compounding even without a new NVIDIA-specific headline; also your largest cross-sector AI holding, so size for that concentration too.

positions.name: IonQ
positions.note: The week's biggest single move in the sector: IonQ raised FY26 revenue guidance to $450–460M (+60% at the midpoint, Sep 17) on its SkyWater foundry acquisition, alongside a CPU-only real-time error decoder and a radar quantum-generative-modeling demo. Shares rose ~16% to $45.48, but the guidance raise still cuts forward P/S to ~40× from ~73× trailing — a genuine risk/reward improvement, not just a price move. Upgraded on that combination; still real optionality with a real chance of zero.

positions.name: Rigetti
positions.note: A quiet week: shares added ~3.5% to $16.66 on broad sector sentiment rather than new company-specific news, and the DARPA Stage B exclusion confirmed last week still stands. Held at the minimum position size — P/S ~417× remains the richest multiple in the sector without a fresh catalyst to justify more.

positions.name: Quantinuum
positions.note: Shares gave back most of last week's rally, falling ~9% to $49.53, even as Quantinuum finalized its $100M CHIPS R&D award and detailed new Oracle and Quanta Computer partnerships. FY26 guidance is still just $28–32M against a ~$13.0B market cap (TTM P/S ~568×), so the pullback doesn't yet close the valuation gap. Held at the minimum; also note the Oracle tie-up sits alongside Microsoft's own AI-sleeve exposure.

positions.name: D-Wave
positions.note: New independent analysis (Trefis, Sep 23) sharpens the case: shares are down ~61% from their 52-week high with no market-wide shock behind it, the $6.48B market cap rests almost entirely on future potential against $3.1M of quarterly revenue, and adjusted EBITDA losses widened 85% YoY to $37.1M. The NTT DOCOMO deployment and BMO Outperform rating are real, but don't yet offset that cash-burn picture.

positions.name: Pasqal
positions.note: Shares fell another ~12% to $6.99 — a fresh post-IPO low, roughly 63% below the Aug 28 debut-day close — despite H1 2026 revenue growth of 14% YoY. No negative company-specific news, just a stock still searching for a floor with limited public financial history. Nothing here changes the case against holding it yet.
